A person does not commit an offence under subsection (1) if, in the case of a licensed restaurant (including a restaurant that is part of licensed accommodation premises) or a licensed public entertainment venue that provides meals—
the liquor is wine, and
the wine was purchased in a bottle or other container at the restaurant or public entertainment venue and was partly consumed at the restaurant or venue, and
the bottle or container is re-corked or otherwise resealed before being carried away.
A person must not obtain, or attempt to obtain, liquor on licensed premises by falsely representing that the person—
is a resident of the premises or a guest of a resident of the premises, or
is intending to eat, or has eaten, a meal on the premises, or
is intending to purchase, or make use of, a product or service provided or supplied on the premises, or
is attending a function on the premises, or
is an employee or agent of the licensee.
Maximum penalty—5 penalty units.
A person must not—
carry liquor about for the purpose of sale, or
offer or expose liquor for sale at or on any place other than a place at or on which liquor may lawfully be sold, or
carry liquor, for the purpose of sale, to a place other than a place at or on which liquor may lawfully be sold.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

If liquor is carried, offered or exposed by a person in contravention of subsection (1) and is so carried, offered or exposed on behalf of another person, that other person is taken to have contravened that subsection.
It is a defence to a prosecution for a contravention of subsection (1) or (2) if it is proved that the liquor was carried, offered or exposed for the purpose of a sale that may lawfully be made.

In the prosecution for an offence under this section, the burden of proving that liquor that has been carried about, or carried to any place, was not so carried for the purpose of sale is on the person charged.

heading.b: Sale of liquor through internet or by other communication media

block.txt: A licensee who sells liquor by taking orders over the telephone or by facsimile or by mail order must cause the licence number to be displayed in any advertisement or information published in writing or electronically in connection with such sales.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

A licensee who sells liquor through an internet site or by other electronic means must ensure that the licence number is prominently displayed on the site or by other electronic means and in any advertisement or information published in writing or electronically in connection with such sales.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A licensee who sells liquor by taking orders over the telephone or by facsimile or by mail order, or who sells liquor through an internet site or by other electronic means—

must, at the time at which an agreement for sale is made, require the prospective purchaser to supply the purchaser’s date of birth so as to confirm that the prospective purchaser is of or above the age of 18 years, unless the prospective purchaser has previously supplied the purchaser’s date of birth to the licensee, and
must give written instructions to the person responsible for delivery of the liquor, requiring that the liquor be delivered—
to the adult person who placed the order, or
to another adult person at those premises who undertakes to accept it on behalf of the person who placed the order, or
if the delivery is made on a day after the day the order is taken—in accordance with the customer’s instructions, or
if the order was sold through an internet site or by other electronic means—to another adult person nominated by the person who placed the order.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
If delivery of any liquor sold in a manner described in this section is taken by a minor—
the delivery is taken to constitute a supply to which section 117(2) applies, and
the licensee, and any person by whom the liquor was delivered on the licensee’s behalf, are each taken to have supplied the liquor contrary to section 117(2).
A licensee who, in accordance with subsection (4), is prosecuted for an offence under section 117(2) has a defence under this subsection if it is proved that the licensee—
complied with the requirements of subsection (3) in relation to the supply concerned, and
at the time of the alleged offence did not know, and could not reasonably be expected to have known, that the alleged offence was committed, and

for a licensee who was a same day delivery provider in relation to the supply of the liquor—had, before the supply occurred, complied with section 114P in relation to the person responsible for delivery of the liquor.
A person (not being a licensee) who, in accordance with subsection (4), is prosecuted for an offence under section 117(2) has a defence under this subsection if it is proved that—

the person to whom the liquor was delivered was of or above the age of 14 years and, before the liquor was delivered, there was produced to the defendant an evidence of age document that may reasonably be accepted as applying to the person and as proving that the person was of or above the age of 18 years, and
at the time of the alleged offence the defendant did not know, and could not reasonably be expected to have known, that the alleged offence was committed, and

for a person who was a same day delivery provider in relation to the supply of the liquor—had, before the supply occurred, complied with section 114P in relation to the person responsible for delivery of the liquor.
A minor must not take delivery of any liquor sold in a manner described in this section unless the minor was ordered or requested by his or her parent or guardian to take delivery of the liquor.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A person must not order or request a minor to take delivery of liquor sold in a manner described in this section.
Maximum penalty—30 penalty units.
This section does not apply to or in respect of the sale of liquor to persons authorised to sell liquor.

heading.b: Responsible service of alcohol training courses

block.txt: In this Division—
approved training course means a training course provided—
by an approved training provider approved by the Secretary in accordance with the regulations in relation to the course, or
by or on behalf of the Secretary.
approved training provider means a training provider approved by the Secretary in accordance with the regulations to provide training courses.

interim certificate means a certificate (in hard copy or electronic form) granted to a person by the Secretary, or by an approved training provider on behalf of the Secretary, following the person’s successful completion of an approved training course, for use by the person in obtaining a recognised competency card.
recognised certification means an interim certificate or a recognised competency card.

recognised competency card means a card issued to a person in accordance with the regulations that certifies as to the matters prescribed by the regulations and provides for the expiry of the card in accordance with the regulations.
training course means a training course prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of section 99(2)(c).

heading.b: Conditions of approval to conduct training courses

block.txt: An approved training provider must comply with such conditions as may be imposed by or under the regulations on the provider’s approval to conduct training courses.
Maximum penalty—
for an individual—50 penalty units, or
for a corporation—250 penalty units.

heading.b: Prohibition on granting interim certificates to unqualified persons

block.txt: An approved training provider must not grant an interim certificate on behalf of the Secretary to any person who has not successfully completed an approved training course conducted by the training provider.
Maximum penalty—
for an individual—50 penalty units, or
for a corporation—250 penalty units.

heading.b: Prohibition on providing training courses without approval

block.txt: A person must not—

provide or offer to provide any training course that is held out, whether directly or indirectly, to be a course that will satisfy the requirements imposed by or under the Act for issue of recognised certification, or
advertise, state or imply in any way that the person is qualified to provide any such course,
unless the person is the Secretary, a person who provides an approved training course on behalf of the Secretary or an approved training provider.
Maximum penalty—
for an individual—50 penalty units, or
for a corporation—250 penalty units.
In this Division—
same day delivery—see section 114F.
same day delivery provider—see section 114G.

In this Division, a same day delivery means the delivery of packaged liquor, under a commercial arrangement, to a person in New South Wales on the same day it is purchased by retail, irrespective of the State or Territory in which the sale is made.
The regulations may prescribe circumstances in which a delivery of packaged liquor is not a same day delivery.
In this Division, a same day delivery provider means a licensee or other person conducting a business or undertaking who, as part of that business or undertaking—
states or otherwise indicates, whether by way of advertisement or otherwise, that the licensee or other person will supply liquor for same day delivery in New South Wales, and
either—
supplies the liquor by way of same day delivery, or
engages an employee or agent to supply the liquor by way of same day delivery.
The regulations may prescribe circumstances in which a licensee or other person is not a same day delivery provider.
A same day delivery provider must not, as part of a same day delivery, supply liquor if the liquor—
is stored for sale at premises within New South Wales, and
is not sold under a licence.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units.
The operation of this provision does not affect the operation of other provisions in this Act that may require a person to obtain a liquor licence to sell liquor in New South Wales.

heading.b: Age to be verified when agreement made for same day delivery

block.txt: A same day delivery provider must, at the time the agreement for the same day liquor delivery is entered into—

use an accredited identity service provider to verify the person entering into the agreement is at least 18 years of age if it is the first time the person has entered into an agreement with the provider, or
use another process, that meets at least the minimum standard prescribed by the regulations, to verify the person’s age.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.

For a second or subsequent occasion on which a person intends to enter into an agreement with a same day delivery provider for the delivery of liquor, the provider must, before entering into the agreement, require the person to undergo a form of authentication prescribed by the regulations.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.
In this section—

accredited identity service provider means an identity service provider who has been accredited under the Trusted Digital Identity Framework published by the Digital Transformation Agency on behalf of the Commonwealth.

heading.b: Evidence of identity and age required for same day deliveries

block.txt: A same day delivery provider must not make a same day delivery to a person, or permit an employee or agent to make a same day delivery for the provider, unless the person produces evidence of the person’s identity and age in a way that complies with the requirements prescribed by the regulations.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.
The regulations may prescribe requirements in relation to the making and keeping of records about evidence of a person’s identity and age produced under subsection (1).

heading.b: Liquor not to be supplied to intoxicated person

block.txt: A person must not, as part of a liquor delivery, supply liquor to an intoxicated person.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units.

It is a defence to a prosecution under subsection (1) for the person who delivered the liquor if it is proved that at the time of the alleged offence the person did not know, and could not reasonably be expected to have known, that the person was delivering liquor.
A courier delivers a package on behalf of an interstate retailer and is unaware the delivery includes liquor.
In this section—
liquor delivery means—
a same day delivery, or
another delivery of packaged liquor, under a commercial arrangement, to a person in New South Wales after it is purchased by retail, irrespective of the State or Territory in which the sale is made.

heading.b: Liquor not to be supplied in alcohol-free zones, alcohol prohibited areas or restricted alcohol areas

block.txt: A person must not, as part of a same day delivery, supply liquor in a public place within—
an alcohol-free zone, or
an alcohol prohibited area, or
a restricted alcohol area.
Maximum penalty—30 penalty units.
This subsection does not prevent liquor being supplied as part of a same day delivery to a person in residential or commercial premises in a zone or area mentioned in paragraph (a)–(c).
In this section—
alcohol-free zone has the same meaning as in the Local Government Act 1993.
alcohol prohibited area means an area declared to be an alcohol prohibited area under section 632A of the Local Government Act 1993.
restricted alcohol area means an area declared to be a restricted alcohol area under Division 2.
A person must not deliver liquor that has been advertised for same day delivery during the period—
starting at—
on a Sunday—11 pm, and
on any other day of the week—midnight, and
ending at 9 am.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units.
The regulations may prescribe deliveries of packaged liquor to which this section does not apply.

heading.b: Records to be kept about refusal to deliver liquor

block.txt: A same day delivery provider must keep a record of a same day delivery that the provider, or an employee or agent of the provider, refuses to make on the grounds that—
by making the delivery the provider, employee or agent would be—
selling or supplying liquor to a minor in contravention of section 117, or
supplying liquor to an intoxicated person in contravention of section 114J, or

at the time of the delivery, the provider, employee or agent was unable to verify the person proposing to accept the delivery was the adult person specified to receive the delivery in the written instructions given by the licensee under section 114(3).
Maximum penalty—30 penalty units.
A same day delivery provider must, if asked by a police officer or inspector—
make a record kept under subsection (1) available for inspection by the police officer or inspector, and
allow the police officer or inspector to take a copy of the record.
Maximum penalty—30 penalty units.
A same day delivery provider must keep a record mentioned in subsection (1) for at least 1 year after the day on which the delivery to which the record relates was to have been made.
Maximum penalty—30 penalty units.

heading.b: Employees and agents not to be penalised for refusal to deliver in particular circumstances

block.txt: This section applies to an employee or agent of a same day delivery provider who makes same day deliveries on behalf of the provider.
The same day delivery provider must ensure the employee or agent does not suffer any financial penalty for refusing to make a same day delivery on the grounds that—
by making the delivery the provider, employee or agent would be—
selling or supplying liquor to a minor in contravention of section 117, or
supplying liquor to an intoxicated person in contravention of section 114J, or

at the time of the delivery, the employee or agent was unable to verify the person proposing to accept the delivery was the adult person specified to receive the delivery in the written instructions given by the licensee under section 114(3).
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.
It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence under this section if it is proved that—
a direction or agreement under which the employee or agent makes same day deliveries on behalf of the same day delivery provider sets out an alternative place for delivery of the liquor, and
the employee or agent did not take reasonable steps to deliver the liquor to that place.
In this section—
financial penalty includes any action that has a financial impact including, for example, withholding or delaying payment or a loss of hours of employment.

A person (the participant) may ask a same day delivery provider to enter into an agreement (a self-exclusion agreement) with the participant under which the participant agrees to be prevented from having liquor delivered by the same day delivery provider to the participant.
A self-exclusion agreement must comply with the requirements prescribed by the regulations.
The same day delivery provider must—
enter into a self-exclusion agreement with the participant, and
comply with the agreement.
Maximum penalty—30 penalty units.
If a same day delivery provider sells or advertises liquor through an internet site or by other electronic means for same day delivery, the provider must ensure that—
the internet site or other electronic means provides a way for a person to enter into a self-exclusion agreement with the provider, and
any person accessing the internet site or other electronic means would reasonably be expected to be alerted to the ability to enter into a self-exclusion agreement.
Maximum penalty—30 penalty units.
No civil or criminal liability is incurred by the same day delivery provider for an act done, or omitted to be done, in good faith and in accordance with this section, in relation to the participant.

heading.b: Training of persons making same day deliveries

block.txt: A same day delivery provider must not make a same day delivery, or permit an employee or agent to make a same day delivery for the provider, unless the provider, employee or agent has the training, that is reasonably practicable, to ensure liquor delivered by the provider, employee or agent as part of a same day delivery is supplied responsibly.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.
Without limiting subsection (1), a same day delivery provider may—
provide an employee or agent of the provider with the training, or
confirm the employee or agent has been provided with the training by another person.

For the purposes of subsection (1), training to ensure liquor delivered by same day delivery providers, and employees and agents, is supplied responsibly must include information that is part of a training program that—
is developed and approved by the Secretary and published on a publicly accessible Government website, and
complies with any minimum requirements for the training prescribed by the regulations under subsection (4)(a).
The regulations may provide for further matters relating to the training of same day delivery providers and providers’ employees or agents, including, for example—
the minimum requirements for the training, and
requirements about testing knowledge of information that is part of the training, and
the provision by the Secretary of training for the purposes of this section.
In this section—
training includes information, instruction and supervision.

heading.b: Same day delivery providers liable for acts of employees and agents

block.txt: This section applies if an employee or agent of a same day delivery provider contravenes—
this Division, or
a regulation made for the purposes of this Division.
The same day delivery provider is taken to have also contravened the provision and is liable to the penalty for a contravention of that provision.
Subsection (1) does not apply if the same day delivery provider has—
ensured the employee or agent has the training referred to in section 114P, and
kept records that demonstrate the provider has complied with paragraph (a).

heading.b: Review of regulation of liquor deliveries

block.txt: The Minister is to review the operation of this Act in relation to the following—
same day deliveries,
other liquor deliveries,
the requirement to provide evidence of age and identity for same day deliveries and other liquor deliveries.
The review under subsection (1)(a) must include consideration of whether—
the policy objectives of the Act in relation to same day deliveries, including rapid delivery, remain valid, and
the terms of this Division remain appropriate for securing the objectives.
The review under subsection (1)(b) must include consideration of—
emerging trends and technologies relevant to liquor deliveries that are not same day deliveries, and
any additional harm minimisation measures that may be appropriate for the liquor deliveries, and
the use of direct and social media marketing and the collection of consumer data to target vulnerable communities.
The review under subsection (1)(c) must include consideration of whether additional evidence of age requirements are needed for liquor deliveries that are not same day deliveries.
A review under this section is to be undertaken as soon as practicable after—
for a review under subsection (1)(a) and (b)—2 years after the commencement of this section, and
for a review under subsection (1)(c)—1 year after the commencement of this section.
A report on the outcome of a review under this section is to be tabled in each House of Parliament within—
for a review under subsection (1)(a) and (b)—6 months after the end of the period of 2 years, and
for a review under subsection (1)(c)—6 months after the end of the period of 1 year.
The regulations may—
declare any area of the State that is specified in the regulations to be a restricted alcohol area for the purposes of this Act, and
restrict the sale, supply, possession or consumption of liquor on any premises (whether or not licensed premises) in any such restricted alcohol area.
Without limiting the restrictions that may be imposed, the regulations may restrict—
the trading hours for licensed premises in a restricted alcohol area, and
the kinds of liquor that may be sold or supplied, and the way in which liquor is sold or supplied, on licensed premises in a restricted alcohol area.
A restricted alcohol area may be declared in respect of an area that is an alcohol-free zone established under the Local Government Act 1993.
A regulation made under this Division has effect despite any other provision of this Act.

For the removal of any doubt, an offence under any other provision of this Act (including Part 2) is not prevented from applying in a restricted alcohol area merely because the regulations create offences for the purposes of this Division.

heading.b: Provisions relating to making of regulations declaring restricted alcohol areas

block.txt: The following provisions apply in relation to any regulation that declares a specified area of the State to be a restricted alcohol area—
the Minister may recommend that the regulation be made only if the Authority, in response to a request by a group of persons—
who are seeking to have the area declared a restricted alcohol area, and
who, in the opinion of the Authority, represent the interests of the community in that area,
has recommended that the area should be declared a restricted alcohol area,
the Authority may not make such a recommendation unless it is satisfied, after consultation with—
the Commissioner for Police, and
the council of each local government area in which the proposed restricted alcohol area would be located, and
if the proposed restricted alcohol area has a recognised Aboriginal community—the Minister for Aboriginal Affairs, and
such other persons as the Authority considers appropriate to consult (including representatives of the community that is likely to be affected by the declaration),
that the proposed regulation is in the public interest and has the support of the majority of the community that is likely to be affected by the declaration.

A regulation made under this Division declaring an area of the State to be a restricted alcohol area must specify a period (not exceeding 3 years) during which the declaration is to have effect. The declaration ceases to have effect at the end of that specified period.
The regulations may prescribe other requirements that must be complied with before an area may be declared to be a restricted alcohol area.

content.txt: pt 6, div 3, hdg: Ins 2012 No 91, Sch 1 [8]. Rep 2017 No 20, Sch 1 [28].

block.txt: In this Division—
high risk venue—see subsection (2).
licensee ban means the exercise by a licensee of premises in a prescribed precinct of a right referred to in section 77(13) to refuse to admit, or turn out, any person from the premises.
long-term banning order means an order under section 116G.
temporary banning order means an order under section 116F.
A high risk venue is a venue situated in a prescribed precinct comprising—
licensed premises—
on which liquor may be sold for consumption on the premises, and
that are authorised to trade after midnight at least once a week on a regular basis, and
that have a patron capacity (as determined by the Secretary) of more than 120 patrons, or
licensed premises specified by, or of a class specified by, the regulations, or
licensed premises that are designated by the Secretary under subsection (4).
The regulations may create exceptions to subsection (2)(a).

The Secretary may, with the concurrence of the Commissioner of Police, designate any specified licensed premises (or licensed premises of a specified class) in a prescribed precinct as a high risk venue if the Secretary is satisfied that there is a significant degree of alcohol-related violence or other anti-social behaviour associated with the premises.
However, the Secretary, when designating premises as a high risk venue, must not take into account the presence of a dance floor or area ordinarily used by patrons for dancing.

The designation of licensed premises as a high risk venue is to be made by order in writing given to the licensee. Any such order takes effect on the date specified in the order (being a date that is not earlier than 6 weeks from the date the order is given).

A decision of the Secretary to designate licensed premises as a high risk venue is reviewable by the Independent Liquor and Gaming Authority under the Gaming and Liquor Administration Act 2007—see section 36A of that Act.
The regulations may declare an area described in the regulations to be a prescribed precinct for the purposes of this Act.
A reference in this Act to premises situated in a prescribed precinct includes a reference to premises—
that front or back onto, or abut, any street or part of a street within the prescribed precinct, or
that can be entered from any such street or part, or
that the regulations declare to be situated in the prescribed precinct.

Except in the case of the Kings Cross precinct, an area may be declared to be a prescribed precinct by reference to a map signed by the Minister and deposited in Liquor and Gaming NSW, Department of Enterprise, Investment and Trade.
Any such maps are to be kept and made available for public access in accordance with arrangements approved by the Minister.

heading.b: Temporary banning orders—licensed premises in prescribed precinct and adjacent precincts

block.txt: A police officer may, in the circumstances described in subsection (2), by order in writing given to a person who is in a prescribed precinct (a temporary banning order) prohibit the person from entering or remaining on any licensed premises in the prescribed precinct and in any other adjacent precinct specified in the order, for the period (not exceeding 48 hours) specified in the order.
A temporary banning order may be made as soon as practicable after the person—

refuses or fails to comply with a direction under section 198 of the Law Enforcement (Powers and Responsibilities) Act 2002 to leave licensed premises in the prescribed precinct or a public place in the vicinity of such licensed premises, or
fails to leave licensed premises in the prescribed precinct after being required to do so under section 77(4) because the person is intoxicated, violent, quarrelsome or disorderly, or
contravenes section 77(6) or (8) in relation to licensed premises in the prescribed precinct.

A police officer must not give a person a temporary banning order unless the officer is satisfied that the conduct of the person which resulted in the person being required to leave (or being refused admission to) the licensed premises or other public place concerned is likely to continue and cause a public nuisance or risk to public safety in the prescribed precinct and in any other adjacent precinct specified in the order.
A temporary banning order—
does not have effect unless it is given by, or given with the approval of, a police officer of or above the rank of sergeant, and
must specify the grounds on which it is given.

A person who is the subject of a temporary banning order must not enter or attempt to enter or remain on any licensed premises in the prescribed precinct or any other adjacent precinct specified in the order during the period specified in the order.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.

A reference in this section to licensed premises does not include a reference to a licensed restaurant that is not authorised to trade after midnight on any day of the week unless it is a high risk venue.

The Authority may, by order in writing (a long-term banning order), prohibit a person from entering or remaining on any high risk venue for such period (not exceeding 12 months) as is specified in the order.
A long-term banning order may only be made on application by the Commissioner of Police in the manner approved by the Authority.
The Authority may make a long-term banning order only if the Authority is satisfied that the person the subject of the proposed order—

has been charged with, or found guilty of, a serious indictable offence involving violence that was committed by the person in a public place or on relevant premises while the person or any victim of the offence was affected by alcohol, or

has been charged with, or found guilty of, a serious indictable offence involving violence that was committed by the person on or in the vicinity of licensed premises and the person was, at the time of the offence—
the licensee or manager of the premises, or

working or performing services of any kind on the premises in the course of any employment (whether paid or unpaid) or in a volunteer capacity, being work or services related to the business carried on under the licence, or
has been given 3 temporary banning orders during a period of 12 consecutive months.

The Authority may not make a long-term banning order unless the person the subject of the proposed order has been given notice of the application for the order and has been given a reasonable opportunity to make submissions to the Authority in relation to the application.

In deciding whether to make a long-term banning order on the ground that a person has been given 3 temporary banning orders, the Authority may take into consideration the circumstances that resulted in the person being given those orders.

A long-term banning order takes effect on the date specified by the Authority in the order. Notice of the making of the order is to be given to the person who is the subject of the order, but failure to give notice does not affect the operation of the order if a reasonable attempt has been made to notify the person.

As soon as practicable after the Authority makes a long-term banning order, the Authority is to provide such persons or bodies (if any) as are prescribed by the regulations with the following information—
the name and address of the person who is the subject of the order,
the period that the order is in force.

A long-term banning order made on the ground that a person has been charged with, or found guilty of, a serious indictable offence is revoked if the charge is withdrawn or dismissed or the finding is overturned on appeal.
A person who is the subject of a long-term banning order must not enter or attempt to enter or remain on any high risk venue during the period specified in the order.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units.
In subsection (3)(a)—
public place includes a place—
of public resort open to or used by the public as of right, or
for the time being—
used for a public purpose, or
open to access by the public,
whether on payment or otherwise, or
open to access by the public by the express or implied permission of the owner of the place, whether the place is or is not always open to the public.
relevant premises means any of the following—
licensed premises,
premises declared under section 3 of the Restricted Premises Act 1943 to be premises to which Part 2 of that Act applies,
premises on which the activities of a criminal group (within the meaning of Division 5 of Part 3A of the Crimes Act 1900) are carried out.

A reference in subsection (3) to a serious indictable offence includes a reference to an offence under the law of another State or Territory that would, had it occurred in New South Wales, have been a serious indictable offence for the purposes of that subsection.

heading.b: Administrative review by Civil and Administrative Tribunal of long-term banning orders

block.txt: A person who is the subject of a long-term banning order may apply to the Civil and Administrative Tribunal for an administrative review under the Administrative Decisions Review Act 1997 of the Authority’s decision to make the order.
Section 53 of the Administrative Decisions Review Act 1997 does not apply in relation to the Authority’s decision to make a long-term banning order.

heading.b: Regulatory controls for licensed premises in prescribed precincts

block.txt: The regulations may prescribe conditions to which a licence relating to premises situated in a prescribed precinct is subject.
Without limiting the matters to which any such conditions may relate, the conditions prescribed by the regulations under this section may—
prohibit or restrict the use of glass or other breakable containers on the licensed premises, or

prohibit or restrict the sale or supply of certain types of liquor on the licensed premises (including liquor with a high alcohol content or liquor that is intended to be consumed rapidly such as a shot), or

prohibit or restrict the sale or supply of liquor on the licensed premises in certain circumstances or at certain times (including in circumstances or at times otherwise permitted by or under this Act), or
prohibit patrons from entering the licensed premises at certain times, or
require the implementation of security or public safety measures in respect of the licensed premises, or
require incident registers to be kept, or

require the exclusion from licensed premises of persons of a specified class (including persons who are wearing any clothing or article displaying the name of, or other matter associated with, a particular organisation), or

require the licensee of any premises situated in the prescribed precinct to contribute towards the costs associated with measures to minimise or prevent alcohol-related violence or anti-social behaviour or other alcohol-related harm in the precinct, or

require the appointment of a person, as approved by the Secretary, who is to be present in a high risk venue during such periods, or in such circumstances, as may be specified or determined by the regulations (an approved manager), or
require records to be kept of the times when an approved manager is present in a high risk venue, or
require records to be kept of the amount of liquor sold or supplied on the licensed premises and require the production of such information.
The conditions that may be prescribed by the regulations under this section may, without limitation, apply to a specified class of licensed premises or to specified licensed premises.

The regulations may authorise the Secretary to exempt the licensee of any premises situated in a prescribed precinct from any of the conditions prescribed by the regulations under this section. The regulations may also provide that any such exemption is subject to conditions specified in the exemption.

The regulations may also authorise the Secretary to declare, by order in writing, any specified part of licensed premises situated in a prescribed precinct to be premises to which the conditions prescribed by the regulations under this section apply.

In approving a person to be present in a high risk venue as required by licence conditions imposed by the regulations under subsection (2)(i), the Secretary must, after obtaining the consent of the person concerned, conduct a criminal record check in relation to the person and be satisfied that the person has the experience and capacity to have responsibility for the high risk venue during the relevant periods. It is the duty of the Commissioner of Police to assist in any such criminal record check.
Any conditions prescribed by the regulations under this section are in addition to any other conditions to which a licence relating to premises in the prescribed precinct may be subject.

Regulations may be made under this section regardless of whether any licensee who is likely to be affected by the regulation has been given an opportunity to make submissions in relation to the proposed regulation.

heading.b: Offences relating to sale or supply of liquor to minors

block.txt: A person must not sell liquor to a minor.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units or 12 months imprisonment (or both).

heading.b: Supplying liquor to minors on licensed premises

block.txt: A person must not supply liquor to a minor on licensed premises.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units or 12 months imprisonment (or both).
It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence under subsection (1) or (2) if it is proved that—
the person to whom the liquor was sold or supplied was of or above the age of 14 years, and

before the liquor was sold or supplied to the person the defendant was provided with an evidence of age document that may reasonably be accepted as applying to the person and as proving that the person was of or above the age of 18 years.

heading.b: Supplying liquor to minors on other premises

block.txt: A person must not supply liquor to a minor on any premises other than licensed premises unless—
the person is a parent or guardian of the minor or is authorised to supply liquor to the minor by a parent or guardian of the minor, and
the supply is consistent with the responsible supervision of the minor.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units or 12 months imprisonment (or both).

The matters that are considered to be relevant in determining whether the supply of liquor is consistent with the responsible supervision of a minor for the purposes of subsection (4) include the following—
the age of the minor,
whether the person supplying the liquor to the minor is intoxicated,
whether the minor is consuming the liquor with food,
whether the person supplying the liquor is responsibly supervising the minor’s consumption of the liquor,
the quantity and type of liquor supplied and the period of time over which it is supplied,
such other matters as may be prescribed by the regulations.
The supply of liquor to a minor who is intoxicated is not, in any circumstances, consistent with the responsible supervision of the minor for the purposes of subsection (4).

Despite subsection (4), a licensee or another person who is delivering packaged liquor on behalf of a licensee or other person that has sold the liquor by retail, irrespective of the State or Territory in which the sale is made, must not supply the packaged liquor to a minor.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units or 12 months imprisonment or both.
It is a defence to a prosecution under subsection (5B) if it is proved that—
the person to whom the liquor was sold or supplied was of or above the age of 14 years, and
before the liquor was sold or supplied to the person the defendant was provided with an evidence of age document
that may reasonably be accepted as applying to the person, and
proving that the person was of or above the age of 18 years.

It is also a defence to a prosecution under subsection (5B) for the person who delivered the liquor if it is proved that at the time of the alleged offence the person did not know, and could not reasonably be expected to have known, that the person was delivering liquor.
A courier delivers a package on behalf of an interstate retailer and is unaware the delivery includes liquor.

heading.b: Obtaining liquor for minors from licensed premises

block.txt: A person must not obtain liquor from licensed premises on behalf of a minor unless the person is the parent or guardian of the minor.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units or 12 months imprisonment (or both).
It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence under subsection (6) if it is proved that the defendant was authorised to obtain liquor on behalf of the minor by the parent or guardian of the minor.

heading.b: Allowing liquor to be sold or supplied to minors on licensed premises

block.txt: A licensee must not, on licensed premises, allow liquor to be sold or supplied to a minor.
Maximum penalty—100 penalty units or 12 months imprisonment (or both).
It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence under subsection (8) if it is proved that the liquor was supplied to the minor by the parent or guardian of the minor.

In the prosecution for an offence under this section, the burden of proving that a person was a parent or guardian of a minor, or was authorised by a parent or guardian of a minor, is on the person charged.
In the application of this section to an on-premises licence that relates to a catering service, a reference to licensed premises does not include any private domestic premises.
For the purposes of this section, supply of liquor includes serving liquor to a person.

heading.b: Offences relating to consumption etc of liquor by minor
Minor not to obtain, consume or carry away liquor

block.txt: A minor must not—
consume liquor on licensed premises, or
consume liquor on the premises of an unlicensed restaurant unless the minor consumes the liquor in the company of, and with the permission of, his or her parent or guardian, or
obtain, or attempt to obtain, liquor for consumption on licensed premises, or
carry liquor away, or attempt to carry liquor away, from licensed premises unless the minor was ordered or requested by another person to carry the liquor away from the licensed premises.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

heading.b: Person not to send, order or request minor to obtain liquor

block.txt: A person must not—
send a minor to licensed premises, or
order or request a minor to go to licensed premises,
for the purpose of obtaining liquor.
Maximum penalty—30 penalty units.
In the application of this section to an on-premises licence that relates to a catering service, a reference to licensed premises does not include any private domestic premises.

heading.b: Licensee not to allow minors to sell or supply liquor on licensed premises

block.txt: A licensee must not cause or allow a minor to sell, supply or serve liquor on the licensed premises except with the approval of the Authority.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.

heading.b: Responsible adult not to allow minor to consume liquor on licensed premises

block.txt: If, under this Act, a minor is required to be accompanied by a responsible adult while in a hotel or on club premises, the responsible adult who is accompanying the minor must not allow the minor to consume liquor on the licensed premises.
Maximum penalty—30 penalty units.
In the prosecution for an offence under this section, the defendant has the burden of proving that he or she was not the responsible adult in relation to the minor at the relevant time.

heading.b: Minors in hotels in company of responsible adult

block.txt: The Authority may, on the application by a hotelier, grant an authorisation (a minors area authorisation) to enable the use by a minor of a specified part of the hotel while in the company of a responsible adult.
Section 51 applies to a minors area authorisation.
The specified part of the hotel to which a minors area authorisation applies may, if the authorisation so provides, comprise the whole of the hotel.

heading.b: Functions for minors in hotels and public entertainment venues

block.txt: In this section—
licensed premises means a hotel or a licensed public entertainment venue.

The Authority may, on application by the licensee concerned, grant an authorisation (a minors functions authorisation) to enable minors to attend a function or functions in a specified part of licensed premises.
Section 51 applies to a minors functions authorisation.

A minors functions authorisation is to designate function areas (that is, each part of the licensed premises on which the functions concerned are permitted to be held) and access areas (that is, each part of the licensed premises through or by means of which persons attending those functions are to be permitted to obtain entry to or to depart from a function area).
Without limiting section 51, a minors functions authorisation is subject to the following conditions—
at least 7 days notice must be given to the local police before any function is held,

the notice must specify the name and nature of the function, the number of minors attending, the number of adult supervisors, details of the security arrangements and such other particulars as may be prescribed by the regulations,
the licensee and person conducting the function must comply with any directions given by the local police or the Authority with respect to the conduct of functions for minors,
liquor must not be sold, supplied, disposed of or consumed in the area in which a function is held,

gaming machines and tobacco vending machines must not be located in the area in which a function is held and any area of the licensed premises in which gaming machines or tobacco vending machines are located must not be accessible to any minor attending the function,
such other conditions as may be prescribed by the regulations.
A licensee is guilty of an offence if any conditions of a minors functions authorisation held by the licensee are contravened.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
Nothing in this section prevents a minors functions authorisation from applying to the whole of the licensed premises concerned.
For the purposes of this section, function includes, but is not limited to, a function as defined in section 4(1).
The Authority may, on application by the holder of a small bar licence, grant an authorisation (a minors authorisation) to enable minors to enter and remain in a small bar.
A minors authorisation for a small bar authorises minors to enter and remain in the small bar—
for the purpose, or in the circumstances, decided by the Authority and stated in the authorisation, and
The Authority may require minors to be in the company of a responsible adult at all times, or during certain times, as a condition of a minors authorisation.
between—
opening time, and
the time, not later than midnight, decided by the Authority and stated in the minors authorisation.
An application for a minors authorisation must—
be made in the form and manner approved by the Authority, and
be accompanied by—
the fee, if any, prescribed by the regulations, and
any information or particulars prescribed by the regulations, and
comply with any other requirements prescribed by the regulations or imposed by the Authority.
In deciding the application, the Authority must—
have regard to any relevant matters prescribed by the regulations, and
refuse to grant the minors authorisation if a mandatory ground for refusing the application prescribed by the regulations applies to the application.

heading.b: Minor not to enter or remain in certain licensed premises

block.txt: A minor must not—
enter or remain in the bar area of a hotel or club premises, or
enter or remain in a part of a hotel to which a minors area authorisation relates unless the minor is in the company of a responsible adult, or
enter or remain in a small bar between 10 am and 10 pm—
unless—
the minor is in the company of a responsible adult, and
meals are regularly provided on the licensed premises at times between opening time and 10 pm when liquor is sold or supplied, and
any other requirements prescribed by the regulations are being complied with, or
unless—
there is a minors authorisation in force for the small bar, and
the minor is in the small bar during the times, and for the purposes or in the circumstances, stated in the authorisation, or
enter or remain in a small bar between 10 pm and midnight unless—
there is a minors authorisation in force for the small bar, and
the minor is in the small bar during the times, and for the purposes or in the circumstances, stated in the authorisation, or
enter or remain in a small bar—
during any period of extended trading between midnight and 5 am on any day of the week, or
during any time that the Authority, by written order given to the licensee, has declared the small bar off-limits to minors, or
enter or remain in a licensed public entertainment venue unless—
the minor is in the company of a responsible adult, or
a function is being held in the venue in accordance with a minors functions authorisation, or
enter or remain in the following areas of licensed premises unless the minor is in the company of a responsible adult—
an area related to a packaged liquor licence,
an area dedicated to the sale of liquor by retail in sealed containers on the licensed premises for consumption away from the licensed premises.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A minor does not commit an offence under subsection (1) if—

the minor is an apprentice or trainee (within the meaning of the Apprenticeship and Traineeship Act 2001) and has entered, or is on, the licensed premises concerned for the purpose only of receiving trade training (not being training in the sale, supply or service of liquor) as such an apprentice or trainee, or

the minor has entered, or is on, the licensed premises concerned for the purpose only of receiving training and instruction in respect of the servicing, repair or maintenance of gaming machines under the supervision of the holder of a technician’s licence within the meaning of the Gaming Machines Act 2001, or
the minor has entered, or is on, the licensed premises for a purpose, or in circumstances, approved by the Authority and specified in the licence under section 124(3)(c).
A minor does not commit an offence under subsection (1)(a) if the minor—

is present in the bar area only for so long as is reasonably necessary to pass through the area in order to conveniently gain access to another area of the hotel or club premises that the minor may enter without contravening this Act, or
is performing in a show or other live entertainment performance held in the bar area,
and is in the company of a responsible adult while in the bar area.
A minor does not commit an offence under subsection (1)(a) in relation to being in the bar area of club premises if—

a reception is being held in the bar area in association with the wedding of a member of the club or of a person who is a child or parent of a member of the club or for whose maintenance a member of the club is or has been responsible, and
the minor has been invited to the reception by a person entitled to issue the invitation.

It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence under subsection (1)(a) or (c) if it is proved that the defendant believed on reasonable grounds that a minors functions authorisation was in force at the relevant time to enable minors to attend a function in a bar area of the hotel or in the public entertainment venue.

It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence under subsection (1)(b1) if it is proved that the defendant believed on reasonable grounds that a minors authorisation was in force at the relevant time to enable minors to enter or remain in the small bar without being in the company of a responsible adult.

Subsection (1)(d) does not apply to an area of licensed premises in which liquor is sold for takeaway or home delivery under a packaged liquor licence that does not authorise the licensee to make walk-up sales.
A minor does not commit an offence under subsection (1)(d) if the minor—
enters or remains in the area of the licensed premises in the minor’s capacity as an employee, and
is not involved in the sale or supply of liquor.

Also, a minor does not commit an offence under subsection (1)(d) if the minor leaves the licensed premises within a reasonable period after being informed by a responsible person that the minor must not be within the area.

It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence under subsection (1)(d) if it is proved that at the time of the alleged offence the minor did not know, and could not reasonably be expected to have known, that the alleged offence had been committed.
A minor is unaccompanied in a bottle shop but is unaware unaccompanied minor must not be within the area.
In the prosecution for an offence under this section, the defendant has the burden of proving that a particular person was the responsible adult in relation to the defendant at the relevant time.

heading.b: Licensee not to allow minors to enter or remain in certain licensed premises

block.txt: If a minor—
enters a bar area of a hotel or club premises, or
enters a part of a hotel to which a minors area authorisation is in force, but is not in the company of a responsible adult, or
enters a small bar between 10 am and 10 pm and—
there is not a minors authorisation in force for the small bar and—
the minor is not in the company of a responsible adult, or
meals are not regularly provided on the licensed premises at times between opening time and 10 pm when liquor is sold or supplied, or
any other requirements prescribed by the regulations are not complied with, or
there is a minors authorisation in force for the small bar but the minor is in the small bar other than during the times, and for the purposes or in the circumstances, stated in the authorisation, or
enters a small bar between 10 pm and midnight and—
there is not a minors authorisation in force for the small bar, or
there is a minors authorisation in force for the small bar but the minor is in the small bar other than during the times, and for the purposes or in the circumstances, stated in the authorisation, or
enters a small bar—
during any period of extended trading between midnight and 5 am on any day of the week, or
during any time that the Authority, by written order given to the licensee, has declared the small bar off-limits to minors, or
enters a licensed public entertainment venue, but is not in the company of a responsible adult, or
enters or remains in the following areas of licensed premises and is not in the company of a responsible adult—
an area related to a packaged liquor licence,
an area dedicated to the sale of liquor by retail in sealed containers on the licensed premises for consumption away from the licensed premises,
the licensee is guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.
If a minor—
is in a bar area of a hotel or club premises, or
is in a part of a hotel to which a minors area authorisation is in force, but is not in the company of a responsible adult, or
is in a small bar between 10 am and 10 pm and—
there is not a minors authorisation in force for the small bar and—
the minor is not in the company of a responsible adult, or
meals are not regularly provided on the licensed premises at times between opening time and 10 pm when liquor is sold or supplied, or
any other requirements prescribed by the regulations are not complied with, or
there is a minors authorisation in force for the small bar but the minor is in the small bar other than during the times, and for the purposes or in the circumstances, stated in the authorisation, or
is in a small bar between 10 pm and midnight and—
there is not a minors authorisation in force for the small bar, or
there is a minors authorisation in force for the small bar but the minor is in the small bar other than during the times, and for the purposes or in the circumstances, stated in the authorisation, or
is in a small bar—
during any period of extended trading between midnight and 5 am on any day of the week, or
during any time that the Authority, by written order given to the licensee, has declared the small bar off-limits to minors, or
is in a licensed public entertainment venue, but is not in the company of a responsible adult, or
is in the following areas of licensed premises and is not in the company of a responsible adult—
an area related to a packaged liquor licence,
an area dedicated to the sale of liquor by retail in sealed containers on the licensed premises for consumption away from the licensed premises,
the licensee is guilty of an offence unless the minor is immediately removed from the area or premises concerned.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.
A licensee does not commit an offence under this section if the minor—

is at least 14 years of age and produces to the licensee (or an employee or agent of the licensee) an evidence of age document that may reasonably be accepted as applying to the minor and as proving that the minor is of or above the age of 18 years, or

is an apprentice or trainee (within the meaning of the Apprenticeship and Traineeship Act 2001) who has entered, or is on, the licensed premises concerned for the purpose only of receiving trade training (not being training in the sale, supply or service of liquor) as such an apprentice or trainee, or
has entered, or is on, the licensed premises concerned for such purposes, or in such circumstances, as may be approved by the Authority and are specified in the licence concerned.
The regulations may prescribe purposes for which, or circumstances in which, the Authority must refuse to grant an approval under subsection (3)(c).
A licensee does not commit an offence under this section in relation to a minor entering, or being or remaining in, a bar area of a hotel or club premises if the minor—

is present in the bar area only for so long as is reasonably necessary to pass through the area in order to conveniently gain access to another area of the hotel or club premises that the minor may enter without contravening this Act, and
is in the company of a responsible adult while in the bar area.
A licensee does not commit an offence under this section in relation to a minor being in the bar area of club premises if—

a reception is being held in that area in association with the wedding of a member of the club or of a person who is a child or parent of a member of the club or for whose maintenance a member of the club is or has been responsible, and
the minor has been invited to the reception by a person entitled to issue the invitation.

A licensee does not commit an offence under this section in relation to a minor being in a licensed public entertainment venue if a function is being held in the venue in accordance with a minors functions authorisation.

It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence under subsection (2)(d) if it is proved that, at the time of the alleged offence, the licensee had taken all reasonable precautions to avoid commission of the alleged offence.
In the prosecution for an offence under this section, the defendant has the burden of proving that a particular person was the responsible adult in relation to a minor at the relevant time.

heading.b: Responsible adult not to leave minor unaccompanied on licensed premises

block.txt: If, under this Act, a minor is required to be accompanied by a responsible adult while in a hotel, small bar, licensed public entertainment venue or packaged liquor premises, the responsible adult who is accompanying the minor must not leave the minor unaccompanied on the licensed premises, or part of the licensed premises, without first informing the licensee or an employee or agent of the licensee.
Maximum penalty—30 penalty units.
In the prosecution for an offence under this section, the defendant has the burden of proving that he or she was not the responsible adult in relation to a minor at the relevant time.
In this section—
packaged liquor premises means an area of licensed premises—
related to a packaged liquor licence, or
dedicated to the sale of liquor by retail in sealed containers on the licensed premises for consumption away from the licensed premises.

heading.b: Minors must be refused entry to licensed premises

block.txt: If—

a responsible person for a hotel, club premises, small bar or licensed public entertainment venue is aware that a person (the relevant person) who may reasonably be suspected of being under the age of 18 years is attempting to enter the licensed premises, and
the presence of the relevant person on the licensed premises would, if the relevant person were under the age of 18 years, be an offence under this Act,

the responsible person must refuse the relevant person entry to the premises unless there is produced to the responsible person an evidence of age document that may reasonably be accepted as applying to the relevant person and as proving that the relevant person is of or above the age of 18 years.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.

heading.b: Notices to be displayed in relation to minors on licensed premises

block.txt: The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the display, on licensed premises or on an internet site or by other electronic means through which a licensee offers liquor for sale, of notices in relation to minors.
Without limiting subsection (1), any such notices may relate to any of the following—
the exclusion of minors from licensed premises or any part of licensed premises,
the presence of minors on licensed premises or any part of licensed premises while in the company of a responsible adult,
the sale of liquor to minors.
The regulations under this section may create offences punishable by a penalty not exceeding 50 penalty units.

A condition that a minor who is 16 years of age or older must be accompanied by a responsible adult must not be imposed by the Authority or the Secretary on a licence in relation to a music festival being held on licensed premises unless the Authority or the Secretary is satisfied the licensee has not put in place sufficient measures to mitigate and manage the risk of minors obtaining liquor on the licensed premises during the music festival.

A person does not contravene this Act or a condition of a licence in relation to a requirement that a minor who is 16 years of age or older must be accompanied by a responsible adult on licensed premises during a music festival if the minor is unaccompanied only for the purposes of attending restroom facilities on the licensed premises.

It is a defence to an offence of contravening a licence condition requiring minors to be accompanied by a responsible adult on licensed premises during a music festival if the licensee made reasonable efforts to ensure minors were accompanied by responsible adults.
Despite the licensee’s reasonable efforts, a minor is unintentionally separated from the minor’s responsible adult at a music festival because of a moving crowd at the festival.
In this section—
music festival has the same meaning as in the Music Festivals Act 2019.
An authorised person may require a person (the relevant person) who is reasonably suspected of being a minor and who, if a minor, would be committing an offence under this Act—
to state the relevant person’s full name, residential address and date of birth, and
to produce then, or at a police station within a reasonable time, an evidence of age document for the person.
A person who is the subject of a requirement under subsection (1) must not—
refuse or fail to state his or her full name, residential address and date of birth, or
without reasonable excuse, refuse or fail to produce an evidence of age document that may reasonably be accepted as applying to the person.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
In this section—
authorised person means a licensee, an employee or agent of a licensee, a police officer or an inspector.

heading.b: Minor must not use false evidence of age

block.txt: A minor who uses any document purporting to be an evidence of age document in order to gain entry to, remain in, or obtain liquor from, licensed premises, is guilty of an offence if the document is false in a material particular in relation to the minor.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A minor may not be imprisoned, or detained in a detention centre, as a consequence of a failure to pay—
a penalty for an offence under this Act or the regulations, or
an amount ordered to be paid under Division 4 of Part 3 of the Fines Act 1996 in respect of a penalty notice issued under this Act.

content.txt: pt 7, div 4: Ins 2014 No 76, Sch 1 [62]. Rep 2020 No 40, Sch 1.1[6].

block.txt: In this part—
food court, for a passenger terminal, means a part of the passenger terminal that—
is not part of licensed premises, and
is set up as—
a food court, or
an area for the consumption of food and drinks, other than an area associated with a single vendor for the consumption of food and drinks from that vendor.
passenger terminal, at an airport, means the parts of the buildings at an airport used for the following—
check-in areas,
arrival or departure areas,
areas where passengers wait after security screening and before boarding a flight.
This section applies to licensed premises in a passenger terminal at an airport.
Despite the provisions of Part 3—
the trading hours of the licensed premises are the lesser of—
the operating hours of the airport, or
if the regulations prescribe reduced trading hours—the reduced trading hours, or
if the Secretary, on the application of the licensee, approves reduced trading hours—the reduced trading hours, and
The Secretary may also reduce trading hours under section 130D for contraventions of this Act or the regulations.
there are no restricted trading days for the licensed premises, and
section 11A does not apply to the licensed premises, and
a requirement that the licensed premises must be open to the general public does not apply, and
a licence that authorises the sale of liquor for consumption on the licensed premises is taken to also authorise the sale of liquor for consumption—
in a food court in the passenger terminal, or
in a seating area associated with the licensed premises, whether inside the passenger terminal or outside.
For section 73 or 117, the food court or seating area must be treated as a part of the licensed premises in relation to liquor sold or supplied under the licence.
A licensee who relies on subsection (2)(e) to sell liquor for consumption in a food court or seating area must ensure that a notice is displayed on the licensed premises—
in a position that is readily able to be read by persons purchasing the liquor, and
that specifies where the liquor may be consumed.
Maximum penalty for subsection (4)—20 penalty units.

heading.b: Duty free and other take-away liquor sales

block.txt: This section applies to licensed premises in a passenger terminal at an airport that has—
an area related to a packaged liquor licence, or
an area dedicated to the sale of liquor by retail in sealed containers on the licensed premises for consumption away from the licensed premises.
Sections 30, 123(1)(d) and 124(1)(d) do not apply to the licensed premises.
The Secretary may modify the application of this part to licensed premises in a passenger terminal at an airport to do one or more of the following—
reduce the trading hours for the licensed premises,
remove or reduce exemptions in this part that relate to minors being permitted to enter licensed premises,
remove or reduce the ability to sell liquor for consumption in a food court or seating area.
The modification may occur if the Secretary is satisfied—
there has been a contravention of this Act or the regulations in relation to the licensed premises, and
the modification is a reasonable response to the contravention.
The Secretary must not make the modification unless the licensee has been given—
written notice of the proposed modification, and
a reasonable opportunity to make submissions to the Secretary about the proposed modification.
A modification is made when the Secretary gives written notice of the modification to the licensee.
The modification commences—
when the notice is given to the licensee, or
if a later date for commencement is specified in the notice—on the later date.
It is a condition of the licence that the licensee comply with this part as modified by the Secretary.
This section applies to licensed premises on land surrounding Western Sydney Airport if the land is prescribed by the regulations.
The Secretary may decide the following despite another provision of this Act—
the trading hours for the licensed premises,
the restricted trading days, if any, for the licensed premises,
whether section 11A applies to the licensed premises.
This section does not affect gaming machine shutdowns under the Gaming Machines Act 2001.
The Authority must give effect to a decision of the Secretary as soon as practicable after being notified of the decision.
A decision of the Secretary may apply to—
particular licensed premises, or
to all or a class of licensed premises.
In this section—
Western Sydney Airport means the land comprising the Sydney West Airport as determined in accordance with the Airports Act 1996 of the Commonwealth and the regulations under that Act.
For this Act, a venue is a live music venue if—
one of the following types of licence is in force for the venue—
a hotel licence,
a club licence,
a small bar licence,
an on-premises licence,
a producer/wholesaler licence, and
live music forms a significant part of the venue’s normal operations.
The regulations may prescribe the circumstances in which live music forms a significant part of a venue’s normal operations.
For this Act, a venue is a live performance venue if the venue—
is a music hall, concert hall, dance hall, theatre or other venue, and
is licensed under an on-premises licence relating to a public entertainment venue, and
is used primarily for live performances or other creative or cultural events, and
is not a live music venue.
For this Act, a venue is a special entertainment precinct venue if—
the venue is located in a special entertainment precinct, and
live music performances or other arts and cultural events—
are held at the venue, or
are intended to be held at the venue and the Secretary has been notified of the intention.
For this Act, a venue is an incentivised event venue if the venue participates in an incentivised event.
In this division—
relevant event means a live music performance or other arts and cultural event meeting the following criteria—
the performance or event is of a duration of 45 minutes or more,
the performance or event is held after—
for a Saturday or Sunday—midday, or
otherwise—6pm.
This section applies to—
a live music venue, or
a live performance venue.
The trading period for the venue is extended by 2 hours after the time that would otherwise apply to the venue under—
section 12, or
an extended trading authorisation.
The 2-hour extension does not apply to the venue unless—
the development consent for the venue permits the extended trading hours, and
a relevant event is held on each day that the venue trades during the 2-hour extended trading period.

heading.b: Special entertainment precinct venues and incentivised event venues

block.txt: This section applies to—
a special entertainment precinct venue, or
an incentivised event venue.
The trading period for the venue is extended by 1 hour after the time that would otherwise apply to the venue under—
section 12, or
an extended trading authorisation.
The 1-hour extension does not apply to the venue unless—
the development consent for the venue permits the extended trading hours, and
for an incentivised event venue—the relevant event is held in conjunction with the incentivised event.
The licensee must ensure that, in any month in which the venue trades during the 1-hour extension, at least 10 relevant events are held at the venue during the month.

heading.b: Records must be kept about extended hours

block.txt: This section applies to a venue if the trading period for the venue is extended under this division.
It is a condition of the licence for the venue that the licensee must keep records of each relevant event held at the venue.
The records must be kept in the form and way approved by the Secretary.
The licensee must, if asked by a police officer or inspector—
make the records available for inspection, and
allow the police officer or inspector to make copies of the records.
To the extent of an inconsistency between a provision of this division and a relevant condition applying to the venue, the provision of this division prevails.
In this section—
relevant condition means a condition prescribed by the regulations under section 116I—

prohibiting or restricting the sale or supply of liquor on licensed premises in certain circumstances or at certain times, including in circumstances or at times otherwise permitted by or under this Act, or
prohibiting patrons from entering licensed premises at certain times.

heading.b: Listed live music and performance venues

block.txt: For this Act, a licensed premises is a listed live music and performance venue if the licensed premises—
is one or more of the following—
a live music venue,
a live performance venue,
a special entertainment precinct venue,
an incentivised event venue, and
is on a list of venues—
kept by the Secretary, and
published on an appropriate government website.
The regulations may prescribe the following—
applications for inclusion on the list, including application fees,
the matters the Secretary must consider in deciding whether to include a venue on the list,
the circumstances in which a venue may be removed from the list,
the procedure for adding a venue to the list or removing a venue from the list.

content.txt: pt 8, div 1, hdg: Ins 2010 No 36, Sch 1 [14].

block.txt: For the purposes of this Act—
local liquor accord means any code of practice, memorandum of understanding or other arrangement that—
affects the supply of liquor, the opening and closing of licensed premises or other aspects of the management of or conduct of business on licensed premises, and
is entered into, in accordance with this Division, for the purpose of eliminating or reducing alcohol-related violence or anti-social behaviour or other alcohol-related harm.

heading.b: Eligible parties to local liquor accord

block.txt: Each of the following bodies or persons may be a party to a local liquor accord and is, for the purposes of this Division, an eligible party—
a licensee,
the Secretary,
the NSW Police Force (to be represented by a police officer nominated by the Commissioner of Police),
a local council,
any body or organisation (such as a Chamber of Commerce) representing commercial or business interests in the relevant local area,
a community or residents’ group with an interest in alcohol-related harm or the amenity of the relevant local area,
any other person or body (or person or body belonging to a class of persons or bodies) prescribed by the regulations.
Any 2 or more eligible parties (at least one of whom is a licensee) may enter into a local liquor accord.
A local liquor accord must include—
the names of the parties to the accord, and
the name and address of the coordinator of the accord (being a party to the accord or the representative of a party), and
the area to which the accord applies, and
any other matter that may be prescribed by the regulations.
The Secretary is to endeavour to ensure that local liquor accords are prepared for, and apply to, all areas of the State.
Without limiting the terms that may be included in a local liquor accord, an accord may make provision for or with respect to any one or more of the following—
authorising or requiring any licensee who is a party to the accord—
to cease to serve liquor (including take-away liquor) on the licensed premises, or
to restrict the public’s access to the licensed premises in a manner and to the extent provided by the accord,
or both, from a time of day that is earlier than the time at which, as required by the relevant licence, trading must cease,
authorising or requiring any licensee who is a party to the accord—
to restrict the use of glass containers, or
to maintain an incident register, or
to install and operate closed-circuit television or any other security device, or
to provide security staff, or
to do any other thing that may be prescribed by the regulations in order to minimise alcohol-related harm.

Entry by any person into a local liquor accord, and any conduct on the part of any person for the purpose of promoting or giving effect to the terms of a local liquor accord, are specifically authorised by this Act for the purposes of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 of the Commonwealth and the Competition Code of New South Wales.

Conduct authorised by subsection (2) is authorised only to the extent (if any) to which the conduct, so far as it consists of things done to regulate the supply of liquor or in some other respect, would otherwise contravene Part IV of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 of the Commonwealth or the Competition Code of New South Wales.

heading.b: Registration and termination of local liquor accord

block.txt: A local liquor accord takes effect when it is registered by the Secretary.
A local liquor accord may be terminated by the parties to the accord.
The termination takes effect when notice in writing of the termination is given by the coordinator of the accord to the Secretary.

heading.b: Requirement to contribute to costs of implementing local liquor accord

block.txt: The Secretary may give a direction to any licensee in the area to which a local liquor accord applies (including any licensee in the area who is not a party to the local liquor accord concerned) to contribute to the costs of promoting or giving effect to the accord.
The licensee is required to comply with any such direction.

heading.b: Precinct liquor accords and community event liquor accords

block.txt: For the purposes of this Act, a precinct liquor accord or a community event liquor accord is a set of measures, approved by the Secretary under this Division, that aim to do either or both of the following—
to minimise or prevent alcohol-related violence or anti-social behaviour, or other alcohol-related harm, in the precinct or area to which the relevant liquor accord applies,

to protect and support the good order or amenity of any such precinct or area in connection with issues arising from the presence of, or any proposed increase in the number of, licensed premises in that precinct or area.

Each of the following persons or bodies may, in accordance with arrangements established by the Secretary, participate in a precinct liquor accord or community event liquor accord (including the development of a proposed liquor accord)—
the licensee for any licensed premises situated in the precinct or area to which the accord applies or is to apply,
the Commissioner of Police,
a local council,
persons who are running businesses or commercial operations in the precinct or area to which the accord applies or is to apply,
a community representative (as approved by the Secretary) for the precinct or area to which the accord applies or is to apply,
